old: Its earliest ancestor, a root meaning 'short,' also quietly shaped a word we now use for feeling cheerful.
It comes from a Latin word, brevis, meaning simply 'short.'
It's a doublet of 'breve' — two English words grown from one Latin seed.
clues: This adjective about time and length shares an ancient root with the cheerful word merry, yet its own meaning has stayed remarkably steady all along.
It describes something lasting only a short while or using few words, like a visit, pause, or remark; unlike plain 'short,' it rarely means physically small. It comes from Latin for short.
As a noun it names a lawyer's written case summary, and in the plural it means snug men's underwear.
